question: What is the primary clinical use of a weighing scale in routine nursing care?

options.A: Assessing nutritional status and tracking fluid balance
options.C: Calculating the total daily calorie intake

explanation: Weight measurements help nurses monitor nutritional health and detect sudden fluid shifts in patients. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why are sudden weight fluctuations particularly dangerous for a patient with heart failure?

options.B: They mean the patient is eating too much salt
options.D: They show an immediate loss of bone mass

explanation: In heart failure, rapid weight gain almost always means the body is holding onto extra fluid that the heart cannot pump out. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h1)

question: Which type of scale is best suited for an adult patient who is completely unable to stand?

options.A: A specialized chair or bed scale

explanation: Chair and bed scales allow nurses to obtain accurate weights for immobile patients without forcing them to stand. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is a major practical advantage of a mechanical beam balance scale over a digital scale?

options.A: It does not require electrical power or batteries
options.B: It is much smaller and easier to carry to field postings
options.C: It automatically calculates the body mass index
options.D: It measures the patient's height at the same time

explanation: Beam balance scales rely purely on mechanical counterweights, making them very reliable in remote clinics where electricity is unreliable. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h2)

question: What should the nurse do first before having a patient step onto a mechanical weighing scale?

options.A: Measure the height of the patient
options.B: Ask the patient to drink a glass of water
options.C: Clean the platform with strong bleach solution
options.D: Check that the scale is zeroed on a flat surface

explanation: Ensuring the scale rests on a hard, level surface and points to zero prevents false readings. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h3)

question: What happens to a weight measurement if a mechanical scale is placed on a thick carpeted floor?

options.A: The reading will be falsely lower than normal
options.B: The reading will be falsely higher than normal
options.C: The scale will lock and refuse to move
options.D: The scale will automatically calibrate itself

explanation: Carpet absorbs some of the downward force from the body, causing the scale to register less weight than the patient actually has. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h3)

question: Why does the nurse keep one hand hovering closely over an infant while they are on the scale pan?

options.A: To add extra downward pressure for accuracy
options.B: To keep the baby warm in a cold clinic room
options.C: To prevent the baby from falling off the scale
options.D: To stop the digital numbers from fluctuating

explanation: Infants make sudden movements and can easily roll off elevated scale pans, making close supervision a vital safety measure. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h4)

question: A mother insists on keeping her baby's heavy winter jacket on during weighing. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Record the weight with the jacket and note it as the true weight
options.B: Explain gently that the jacket must be removed for an accurate weight
options.C: Weigh the baby with the jacket and subtract an estimated guess
options.D: Refuse to weigh the baby until the next clinic visit

explanation: Heavy clothing adds significant extra weight, so infants should be weighed naked or with minimal clothing like a dry diaper. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h4)

question: Where should the patient stand on the platform during a weight measurement?

options.A: Leaning against the wall for proper balance
options.B: As far forward as possible to see the numbers
options.C: In the exact center with weight distributed evenly
options.D: With one foot on the floor for stability

explanation: Standing centrally with balanced footing ensures the entire body mass rests squarely on the weighing mechanism. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h5)

question: What is a parallax error when reading a scale, and how do you prevent it?

options.A: An error caused by the patient wearing heavy rubber shoes
options.B: An inaccurate reading caused by looking at the scale from an angle instead of straight at eye level
options.C: A mechanical failure caused by sliding the heavy counterweight too fast
options.D: A false measurement resulting from an unlevel floor surface

explanation: Looking at a scale from above or below skews the numbers. Always read the measurement directly at eye level to get it right! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h5)

question: Why are serial weight measurements over several months more useful than a single isolated measurement in children?

options.A: They show the actual growth velocity and long-term nutritional trend
options.B: They correct for any errors made by the scale manufacturer
options.C: They eliminate the need to measure the child's height
options.D: They prevent the child from moving around during the visit

explanation: Growth is a dynamic process, and plotting multiple weights on a growth chart reveals whether a child is developing normally over time. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h6)

question: Which patient might have a high Body Mass Index (BMI) classification that does NOT accurately reflect excess body fat?

options.A: An elderly patient experiencing severe muscle wasting
options.B: A malnourished child with chronic protein deficiency
options.C: A professional weightlifter with high muscle mass
options.D: A sedentary patient with advanced kidney disease

explanation: Muscle tissue is much denser than fat, meaning very muscular people can have a high BMI despite having low body fat. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h6)

question: When is the best time to clean and disinfect a clinical weighing scale?

options.A: Only when visibly soiled with body fluids
options.C: Once every week during routine cleaning
options.D: Only at the end of the work shift

explanation: Wiping the scale after each patient prevents the spread of skin infections and germs. Excellent infection control practice! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h7)

question: What is the primary risk of pouring liquid disinfectant directly onto a digital weighing scale?

options.A: Liquid can seep inside and damage internal electronic circuits
options.B: It permanently locks the zero-adjustment mechanism
options.C: It causes the exterior paint to change color immediately
options.D: It will make the metal platform slippery for the next patient

explanation: Moisture inside electronic devices causes short circuits and rust, so nurses should use damp disinfectant wipes rather than pouring liquid. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h7)
